Directions: Read the following sentence and find out the part that has an error in it. If the sentence is error-free, choose 'no error' as your answer.

I reminded my brother to buy the tickets (A) for the game that were available last week, (B) but he missed that boat by waiting till today (C) to buy and now all the tickets are sold out. (D)
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 3.

Key Points

The part that contains the error is (C) i.e. 'but he missed that boat by waiting till today'.

  • After reading the given sentence we can conclude that the sentence is grammatically correct but in part (C) of the sentence there is an idiom used i.e. missed that boat which is used incorrectly.
  • The correct idiom is 'missed the boat' which means to be too slow to take advantage of an opportunity and it is used in the context of missing the opportunity to by the tickets in the given sentence.
  • Therefore, the correct sentence would be 'I reminded my brother to buy the tickets for the game that were available last week, but he missed the boat by waiting till today to buy and now all the tickets are sold out.'
 
Additional Information
  • What is an Idion?
  • An Idiom is a group of words established by usage as having a meaning not deducible from those of the individual words.
    • For Example -
  • Over the moon - extremely happy; delighted.
    • I was over the moon to see my family after a long time.
  • Piece of cake - something easily achieved
    • Starting your own business is no piece of cake.

Directions: Read the following sentence and find out the part that has an error in it. If the sentence is error-free, choose 'no error' as your answer.

The security guards of the city museum were very vigilant (A) yet did not saw the thieves coming in (B) from the front door of the museum and stealing (C) valuable objects of great historic significance. (D)
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 2.Key Points

The part that contains the error is (B) i.e. 'yet did not saw the thieves coming in'.

  • Here, the given sentence is in the past simple tense, and part (B) of the sentence is a negative sentence of past simple tense.
  • Sentence structure of negative sentences in past simple tense - 
  • Subject + did not + base form of verb + object 
    • For Example - 
    • He did not drink coffee.
    • My father did not come to my restaurant's opening.
  • Thus, we can conclude that verb (saw) in part (B) should come in its base/first form and it is given in its second form which is incorrect, while the rest of the sentence is correct.
  • Therefore, the correct sentence would be 'The security guards of the city museum were very vigilant yet did not see the thieves coming in from the front door of the museum and stealing valuable objects of great historic significance.'
 
Additional Information
  • Let's look at the important vocab given in the sentence - 
  • 1) Vigilant = keeping careful watch for possible danger or difficulties (चौकन्ना)
  • 2) Significance = the quality of being worthy of attention; importance (महत्व)
  • 3) Historic = famous or important in history, or potentially so (ऐतिहासिक)

Read the following sentence and determine whether there is any error in it. The error, if any, will be in one part of the sentence. If the sentence is error-free, select ‘No error’ as your answer.

More than one (A)/ student in our class (B)/ have learned a lot (C)/ for the final examination.(D)/
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is C- the error lies in this part.

Key Points

  • The error lies in part A of the sentence.
  • ​In a sentence, the verb is used according to person and number.
  • In the case of the following words, the verbs used will be singular:
    • Each, every/everyone, someone/somebody, none/ nobody, one, no one, any, many a, more than one, etc.​​
  • Example:9
    • Everyone are addicted to smartphones nowadays. (Incorrect)
    • Everyone is addicted to smartphones nowadays. (Correct)
  • As the main subject in the given sentence is 'More than one', the verb will also be singular i.e. was.
  • Since the given structure is already followed in the given question, the 3rd option i.e. C will be the correct choice.
     

Correct Sentence: More than one student in our class has learned a lot for the final examination.  

Additional Information

  • A singular verb is used when two nouns that are qualified by ‘each’ and ‘every’ are joined by the conjunction ‘and’.
  • Let’s see an example-
    • Every man and every woman in the neighborhood has to give their best to make tomorrow's program a success.  (Correct)
    • Every man and every woman in the neighborhood have to give their best to make tomorrow's program a success.  (Incorrect)

Hint

  • The determiner 'more than one' will decide the verb - singular or plural. In the case of more than one, the verbs used will be singular.

questions.text: Choose the synonym of the word 'Ominous'.

  • Let's look at the meaning of the given options:-
    • Menacing - Suggesting the presence of danger; threatening.(भयभीत करनेवाला)
      • Example: The fraud is always more menacing than the real thing.
    • Promising - Pointing toward a happy outcome.(आशाजनक
      • Example: All the signs for the new business are promising.
    • Propitious - Giving or indicating a good chance of a happy outcome; auspicious.(अनुकूल)

    • Auspicious - Something that seems likely to be successful in the future.(शुभ)
      • Example: No party could have hoped for a more auspicious start to an election campaign.
    • Providential - Occurring at a favorable time; opportune.(दैवीय संयोग)
      • Example: Their departure just before the floods was providential.
         

Hence, the only possible answer is option 1.

Additional Information

When two bodies A and B are moving with speed ‘a’ kmph and ‘b’ kmph respectively, then the relative speed of two bodies is

(i) (a + b) kmph if they are moving in opposite direction

(ii) (a - b) kmph if they are moving in same direction

Time taken to meet each other = distance between them / relative speed

Calculation:

Relative speed of jerrry and tom = speed of tom - speed of jerry

questions.text: Meena’s capital is 2/3 times more than Mira’s capital. Mira invested her capital at 40% per annum for 2 years (compounded annually). At what rate of interest per annum at simple interest should Meena invest her capital so that after 2 years, they both have the same amount of capital?
questions.explanation:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of Meena’s capital to Mira’s capital = (1 + 2/3) : 1 = 5 : 3.

Mira’s Amount factor after 2 years at 40% CI = (1.4)2 = 1.96.

Total Amount for Mira = 3 × 1.96 = 5.88 units.

Meena’s interest needed = 5.88 − 5 = 0.88 units.

Rate (SI) = (Interest ÷ Principal × Time) × 100 = (0.88 ÷ 5 × 2) × 100 = 8.8%.

∴ The correct answer is 8.8%.

Alternate Method

Given: Meena’s Capital (P1) is 2/3 more than Mira’s Capital (P2).

⇒ Let P2 = 300, then P1 = 300 + (2/3 × 300) = 500.

⇒ Mira’s Amount (A2) at 40% Compound Interest for 2 years:

⇒ A2 = 300 × (1 + 40/100)2 = 300 × (1.4)2

⇒ A2 = 300 × 1.96 = 588.

⇒ For Meena, Amount (A1) = 588 at Simple Interest for 2 years:

⇒ SI = A1 − P1 = 588 − 500 = 88.

⇒ SI = (P × R × T) / 100 ⇒ 88 = (500 × R × 2) / 100

⇒ 88 = 10 × R ⇒ R = 8.8%.

∴ The correct answer is 8.8%.

Additional Information

Compound Interest Amount

The formula for amount in Compound Interest is A = P(1 + r/100)n, where n is the number of years.

Simple Interest Formula

Interest in Simple Interest is calculated only on the principal: SI = (P × R × T) / 100.

Successive Percentage for CI

Effective rate for 2 years at r% CI is (r + r + r2/100)%. For 40%, it is 40 + 40 + 16 = 96%.

questions.text: A container contains 60 liters of milk. Ramu a dishonest milkman decided to mix water in the mixture. From this container, 6 liters of milk was taken out and replaced by water. This process was further repeated two times. How much milk is left in the container in the end of the total replacements?
questions.explanation:
Shortcut Trick

Remaining quantity of milk = Initial quantity × (1 − Replaced quantity ÷ Total capacity)n

Here, Initial quantity = 60 liters, Replaced quantity = 6 liters, and number of operations n = 3.

Ratio of remaining milk = (1 − 6 ÷ 60)3 = (9 ÷ 10)3 = 0.729

Remaining milk = 60 × 0.729 = 43.74 liters.

∴ The correct answer is 43.74 litre.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial quantity of pure milk = 60 liters

Quantity of milk replaced in each cycle = 6 liters

Total number of operations (n) = 1 (initial) + 2 (further) = 3 times

Formula Used:

Remaining Milk = PV × (1 − x ÷ V)n

Where, PV = Initial volume of milk, x = Volume replaced in each step, V = Total volume of the container, n = Number of times the process is repeated.

Calculations:

⇒ Remaining Milk = 60 × (1 − 6 ÷ 60)3

⇒ Remaining Milk = 60 × (1 − 1 ÷ 10)3

⇒ Remaining Milk = 60 × (9 ÷ 10)3

⇒ Remaining Milk = 60 × (729 ÷ 1000)

⇒ Remaining Milk = 6 × 7.29

⇒ Remaining Milk = 43.74 liters

∴ The correct answer is 43.74 litre.

Additional Information

Repeated Dilution Formula

questions.text: In a family of four members A, B, C, and D, Rs. 50,000 was divided among them. A took 2/3 of the money, B took 1/5 of the remaining amount, and the rest was divided between C and D in the ratio of 2 : 3 respectively. How much(approx.) did C get as his share?
questions.explanation:
Shortcut Trick

Total amount = ₹50,000

Remaining after A = 1 − 2/3 = 1/3

Remaining after B = 1/3 × (1 − 1/5) = 1/3 × 4/5 = 4/15

Share of C = 4/15 × 2/5 = 8/75 of total

C's share = 50,000 × 8/75 = 2,000 × 8/3 = 16,000/3 ≈ ₹5,333.33

∴ The correct answer is ₹5,334.

Alternate Method

Given: Total = ₹50,000 | A's share = 2/3 | B's share = 1/5 of remaining | C : D = 2 : 3

⇒ Share of A = 50,000 × 2/3 = ₹33,333.33

⇒ Remaining amount = 50,000 − 33,333.33 = ₹16,666.67

⇒ Share of B = 16,666.67 × 1/5 = ₹3,333.33

⇒ Amount left for C and D = 16,666.67 − 3,333.33 = ₹13,333.34

⇒ Ratio C : D = 2 : 3 (Total parts = 5)

⇒ Share of C = (2/5) × 13,333.34

⇒ Share of C = ₹5,333.336 ≈ ₹5,334

∴ The correct answer is ₹5,334.

Additional Information

Ratio and Proportion

If an amount X is divided in ratio a:b, then share of first part = [a/(a+b)] × X.

Successive Fractions

When dealing with remainders, the final remaining fraction is (1 − f1) × (1 − f2) × ... × (1 − fn).

questions.text: Average age of P, Q and R is 90 years. When S joins them the average age becomes 86 years. A new person T whose age is 6 years more than S, replaces P and the average of Q, R, S and T becomes 84 years. What is the age of P?
questions.explanation:
Given :

Average age of P, Q, and R = 90 years

Average age of P, Q, R and S = 86 years

Average age of Q, R, S and T = 84 years

Formula Used :

Average = Sum of observation/No. of observation

Shortcut Trick

The age of S = Sum of age of P, Q, R, S - Sum of age of P, Q, R

The age of S = 86 × 4 - 90 × 3 = 74 years

The age of T = 74 + 6 = 80 years

The age of P = Sum of age of P, Q, R, S, T - Sum of age of Q, R, S, T

The age of P = 86 × 4 + 80 - 84 × 4 = 424 - 336 = 88 years

∴ Age of P is 88 Years

Alternate Method

Calculation :

Average age of P, Q, and R = 90 years

⇒ (P + Q + R)/3 = 90

⇒ P + Q + R = 270

Similarly, Average age of P, Q, R and S = 86 years

⇒ (P + Q + R + S)/4 = 86

⇒ P + Q + R + S = 344

⇒ Age of P, Q, and R + Age of S = 344

⇒ 270 + S = 344

⇒ S = 74 years

If the age of S is 74 year

Then the Age of T = 74 + 6 = 80 years

Similarly, Average age of Q, R, S and T = 84 years

⇒ (Q + R + S + T)/4 = 84

⇒ Q + R + S + T = 84 × 4

⇒ Q + R + S + T = 336

⇒ Q + R + 74 + 80 = 336 (Putting the value of S, and T)

⇒ Q + R = 182

⇒ Age of P, Q, and R = 270

⇒ P + Q + R = 270 (Putting the value of Q + R from above)

⇒ P + 182 = 270

⇒ P = 88 years

∴ Age of P is 88 Years.

questions.text: Which of the following environmental phenomena is a direct result of chemical runoff from agricultural fertilizers and pesticides reaching coastal waters, leading to severe oxygen depletion?

options.text: Creation of hypoxic aquatic dead zones
Increase in the solubility of dissolved oxygen
Production of primary microplastics via bioaccumulation

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Creation of hypoxic aquatic dead zones

Key Points

  • Dead Zones: These are oxygen-depleted areas in aquatic environments where oxygen levels fall so low that most marine life cannot survive. This condition is often referred to as hypoxia.
  • Agricultural Runoff: Fertilizers and pesticides used in farming contain high levels of inorganic nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus. When these are washed into rivers and eventually reach the ocean, they trigger the process of eutrophication.
  • The Process: The excess nutrients lead to rapid algal blooms. As these algae die and decompose, bacteria consume the available dissolved oxygen in the water to break down the organic matter. This depletion results in hypoxic conditions.
  • Marine Impact: In coastal environments, this nutrient runoff is a primary driver for the formation of dead zones, disrupting marine reproduction and leading to the death of aquatic organisms.

Additional Information

  • The largest known dead zone is located in the Arabian Sea's Gulf of Oman, covering approximately 63,700 square miles.
  • The Gulf of Mexico in the USA is home to the second-largest dead zone in the world, primarily due to nutrient discharge from the Mississippi River.
  • Other related phenomena include "Red Tides" (algal blooms that discolor water) and "Blue Tides" (caused by luminescent phytoplankton), both of which indicate degraded ecosystems with high nitrogen levels.

Important Points

  • Geogenic causes: These refer to naturally occurring processes, such as the sedimentary deposits that release arsenic into groundwater, rather than chemical runoff from human activity.
  • Oxygen Solubility: Factors like thermal pollution actually reduce the solubility of oxygen in water, rather than increasing it.
  • Microplastics: These are physical pollutants (either manufactured as microbeads or resulting from the degradation of larger plastic items) and are not a chemical product of agricultural fertilizer runoff.

questions.text: Which type of agriculture is suitable for high land area of equatorial region?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Plantation agriculture.

Key Points

  • The tropical plantation is one of the world’s oldest systems of commercial agriculture. Since 1500 AD, the products from over a dozen tropical crops have been in constant demand by people in the temperate regions.
    • The specialized commercial cultivation of cash crops on estates or plantations is a very distinctive type of tropical agriculture and is found in many parts of Asia, Africa, and tropical and sub-tropical America.
    • Plantation agriculture is the product of colonialism. Plantations have been developed in response to a demand in Europe for foods, spices, fibres, and beverages, which because of climatic constraints, could be produced only in the tropics or sub-tropics.

Additional Information

  • Humid Farming: Humid farming is prevalent in areas where rainfall is abundant, excess water is stored and provided to the farmlands — systematically. The rainy season is the sowing season, harvesting is done in the dry months.
    • Humid farming is practised all over monsoon-Asia, Tropical Africa, and Mediterranean regions.
  • Dry farming, also called Dryland Farming, the cultivation of crops without irrigation in regions of limited moisture, typically less than 20 inches (50 centimetres) of precipitation annually.
    • Dry farming depends upon efficient storage of the limited moisture in the soil and the selection of crops and growing methods that make the best use of this moisture.
    • Tilling the land shortly after harvest and keeping it free from weeds are typical methods, but in certain latitudes, stubble is left in the fields after harvest to trap snow.
    • Moisture control during crop growing consists largely of the destruction of weeds and prevention of runoff.
    • The ideal soil surface is free of weeds but has enough clods or dead vegetable matter to hinder runoff and prevent erosion.
  • Commercial agriculture is a large-scale production of crops for sale, intended for widespread distribution to wholesalers or retail outlets. In commercial farming crops such as wheat, maize, tea, coffee, sugarcane, cashew, rubber, banana, cotton are harvested and sold in the world markets.

questions.text: Within the classification of silvopastoral systems, what characterizes the management and primary purpose of a Fodder Bank?

options.text: Dense, intensively managed plantings of highly nutritious fodder trees and shrubs intended for cut-and-carry livestock feed
The seasonal storage of dried crop residues and grains in underground pits for livestock during droughts
A system of unmanaged, random woody growth in natural rangelands where livestock graze freely
The integration of nitrogen-fixing trees specifically to enhance the growth of aquatic plants for fish feed

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Dense, intensively managed plantings of highly nutritious fodder trees and shrubs intended for cut-and-carry livestock feed

Key Points

  • Definition: A Fodder Bank is a specialized silvopastoral system consisting of dense and intensively managed plantings of highly nutritious trees and shrubs.
  • Mechanism: Unlike free-range grazing, Fodder Banks are specifically intended for a cut-and-carry management system. This means the vegetation is harvested by the farmer and brought directly to the livestock.
  • Component Choice: The species selected for these banks are typically chosen for their high nutritional value to improve animal health and productivity.
  • Classification: It falls under Silvopastoral Systems, which intentionally combine woody perennials with livestock components to optimize land use.

Additional Information

  • Silvopastoral Variations: Apart from Fodder Banks, other systems include Trees on Pasture (where trees provide shade and shelter for grazing animals) and Live Fences (where trees act as biological barriers while providing fodder).
  • Management Practices: To maintain high productivity in a Fodder Bank, practices like pollarding or coppicing (repeated cutting to promote new growth) are often employed.
  • Multipurpose Trees (MPTs): Many trees used in fodder banks serve multiple roles, such as providing nitrogen fixation to the soil while offering high-protein leaves for feed.

Important Points

  • Comparison with other options:
    • Option 2 describes physical storage of dry materials, not a living agroforestry planting system.
    • Option 3 contradicts the principle of Intentional Integration, which requires deliberate management rather than random growth.
    • Option 4 describes a characteristic more aligned with Aquaforestry or general soil improvement rather than the specific definition of a Fodder Bank.
  • Objective: The primary goal of a fodder bank is to ensure a stable supply of high-quality feed, especially during dry seasons when natural pastures may be insufficient.

Nitrogen is generally low, but potash, phosphoric acid, and alkalis are adequate.

Black soils

Black soil is of red color mainly due to its iron oxide content.

Laterite soils are rich in iron and aluminum but deficient in nitrogen and potassium.

questions.text: What is the primary cause for the characteristic red color found in Red and Yellow soils?

options.text: Accumulation of high organic humus content in the topsoil
Presence of calcium carbonate nodules known as kankar
Diffusion of iron from crystalline igneous parent rocks
Intense leaching of silica due to heavy tropical rainfall

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Diffusion of iron from crystalline igneous parent rocks

Key Points

  • Red and Yellow soils are formed from the weathering of crystalline igneous rocks, particularly in regions characterized by low rainfall.
  • The distinct red color of these soils is specifically attributed to the diffusion of iron from these crystalline igneous parent rocks.
  • A notable characteristic of this soil type is its color change; when the soil is in a hydrated form, it appears yellow rather than red.
  • In terms of chemical composition, these soils are typically deficient in nitrogen, phosphorus, and organic matter (humus), which impacts their natural fertility.

Additional Information

  • Distribution: These soils are widely distributed across the Deccan Plateau, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, and parts of the Middle Ganga Plain.
  • Texture and Fertility: The fertility of Red and Yellow soils varies significantly with texture; fine-grained varieties are generally fertile and suitable for agriculture, while coarse-grained varieties found in dry uplands are less productive.
  • Crystalline Igneous Rocks: These are rocks like granite or gneiss that form from the cooling of molten rock and possess a crystal structure. The iron within these minerals oxidizes and diffuses, giving the soil its pigment.

Important Points

  • Comparison with Arid Soils: Unlike Red soils, Arid soils are characterized by high salt content and the formation of 'kankar' (calcium nodules) which can hinder water infiltration.
  • Comparison with Laterite Soils: While both contain iron, Laterite soils form under high rainfall and temperature through intense leaching, making them rich in aluminum as well as iron.
  • Comparison with Peaty Soils: Peaty soils are rich in organic content (40-50%) and are black in color, contrasting sharply with the mineral-heavy, iron-rich Red soils.

questions.text: Which of the following describes the specific size and origin of nanoplastics in the marine environment?

options.text: Plastic debris larger than 5 mm that enters the ocean through land-based urban runoff
Plastic particles smaller than 100 nm formed by the further environmental degradation of microplastics
Manufactured plastic items like microbeads used in cosmetics that are smaller than 5 mm
Synthetic polymers larger than 100 nm that are specifically designed for industrial shipping use

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Plastic particles smaller than 100 nm formed by the further environmental degradation of microplastics

Key Points

  • Nanoplastics are specifically classified as plastic particles with a size smaller than 100 nm.
  • They represent a further stage of environmental breakdown, typically formed when microplastics (which are already smaller than 5 mm) undergo continuous degradation through processes like photodegradation or hydrolysis.
  • Unlike macroplastics (larger than 5 mm) or microplastics (smaller than 5 mm), nanoplastics are so minute that they pose unique challenges for detection and environmental monitoring.
  • Microplastics themselves are categorized into primary microplastics (manufactured as small beads) and secondary microplastics (degraded from larger items). Nanoplastics are essentially the byproduct of secondary microplastic fragmentation.

Additional Information

  • Marine plastic pollution is considered a "planetary crisis" by the United Nations, with approximately 14 million tons of plastic entering the oceans every year.
  • The accumulation of these plastics often leads to the formation of massive garbage patches, such as the North Pacific Garbage Patch, which is the largest in the world.
  • Because of their extremely small size, nanoplastics and microplastics can easily be ingested by marine organisms, leading to bioaccumulation and biomagnification throughout the food chain, eventually reaching humans.
  • These particles can also leach toxic chemicals, which may affect the reproduction, growth, and survival of various marine species.

Important Points

  • Macroplastics: Items larger than 5 mm (e.g., plastic bags, bottles).
  • Microplastics: Items smaller than 5 mm (e.g., microbeads, fragmented bits).
  • Nanoplastics: Particles smaller than 100 nm (formed from further microplastic degradation).
  • The primary environmental concern regarding nanoplastics is their ability to penetrate biological membranes due to their microscopic scale.

questions.text: Which soil horizon is primarily composed of partially disintegrated and weathered parent rock material and is characterized by having minimal biological activity?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is C Horizon

Key Points

  • C Horizon (Parent Material): This layer consists of partially disintegrated and weathered rock fragments. It is the fundamental layer from which the process of soil formation begins.
  • Biological Activity: A defining characteristic of the C horizon is that it possesses minimal biological activity, distinguishing it from the nutrient-rich upper layers.
  • B Horizon (Subsoil): Unlike the C horizon, the B horizon is defined by the accumulation of minerals such as iron, aluminum, and clay that have leached down from upper layers. It is important for moisture retention.
  • R Horizon (Bedrock): Positioned below the C horizon, this layer consists of unweathered, solid parent rock that has not yet been broken down into smaller particles.

Additional Information

  • Soil horizons are distinct horizontal layers developed through the continuous process of pedogenesis, involving physical, chemical, and biological forces over long periods.
  • The C horizon serves as the link between the solid bedrock (R horizon) and the more developed soil layers (A and B horizons) above it.
  • While horizons like the A horizon (topsoil) support intense biological activity and plant root growth, the C horizon lacks the organic matter required for such activity.

Important Points

  • O Horizon: Topmost organic layer rich in humus.
  • A Horizon: Topsoil where most biological activity occurs.
  • E Horizon: Eluviation layer where minerals are leached downward.
  • B Horizon: Subsoil where minerals and clay accumulate.
  • C Horizon: Parent material consisting of weathered rock with low biological activity.
  • R Horizon: Solid, unweathered bedrock.
